title: Affine even-moment coefficient expansion
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mu$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r\in\mathbb N$. Suppose that $\mathbb E_\mu[X^{2l-1}]=0$ for every integer $l$ with $1\le l\le r$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. Then
\[
\mathbb E_\mu\!\left[(1+\sigma_r tX)^{2r}\right]-(1+t^2)^r
=\sum_{l=0}^{r}\Delta_{r,l}(\mu,X)t^{2l},
\]
where $\sigma_r=1/\sqrt{2r-1}$ and $\Delta_{r,l}(\mu,X)=\binom{2r}{2l}\sigma_r^{2l}\mathbb E_\mu[X^{2l}]-\binom rl$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
Odd moments vanish: $\mathbb E_\mu[X^{2l-1}]=0$ for $1\le l\le r$
